description:
SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 

  Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF)  
  Contracting Department (Code 400)  
  Requirement:  Confidence Testing, Inspection, and Certification of ANSUL Automatic CO2 Fire Suppression System 
  Document / PR Number:  N4523A12956436 

  

 1. GENERAL INFORMATION & NOTICE DISCLAIMER 

 THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS NOTICE IS ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR INVITATION FOR OFFERORS TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS. A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR OFFERORS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. 

 The Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), Contracting Department (Code 400), is issuing this sources sought notice. The sources sought is being issued as a means of conducting market research to determine the interest, availability, and capability of Industry to participate in a competitive acquisition for semi-annual confidence testing, inspection, certification, emergency trouble calls, and repair services for an  ANSUL Automatic  CO2  Fire Suppression System  protecting an industrial plant varnish dip tank system in Building 427 at PSNS & IMF, Bremerton, WA. 

 The tentative North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code selected for this acquisition is  561621 (Security Systems Services - Fire Alarm Systems Sales/Installation/Servicing) , , with an applicable Small Business Size Standard of 25.0M (for NAICS 561621). To be considered an interested vendor, your company should possess the applicable NAICS code in your System for Award Management (SAM) profile. Interested offerors must be active and registered in SAM at www.sam.gov. 

 Based on the responses received to this sources sought notice, this requirement may be set-aside for small business (in full or in part), procured through full and open competition (unrestricted), or procured on a sole-source basis. All small business set-aside categories (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], and Women-Owned Small Business [WOSB]) will be considered. 

 Telephonic inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged. The Government will not provide evaluations, debriefs, or formal comments to companies providing sources sought responses; however, the responses received will be used to inform the Government as to the best means of procuring this requirement. FURTHER SPECIFICATIONS AND DETAILS WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE FORTHCOMING REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ). 

  

 2. SUMMARY OF REQUIREMENT & SCOPE OF WORK 

 
	  Objective:  The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and non-personal services to perform semi-annual confidence testing, inspection, and certification on an ANSUL Automatic CO2 Fire Suppression System, as well as handle emergency trouble calls and unscheduled repairs. 
	  Protected Equipment:  The system protects critical industrial plant equipment (varnish dip tank system) supporting the dipping and coating of electric motor components in Shop 51. Scheduled and potential emergent fleet support requires the system to maintain a state of continuous operational readiness. 
	  Place of Performance:  Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF, 1400 Farragut Ave, Bremerton, WA 98314, Building 427, at Column 34. 
	  Period of Performance:  Semi-annual service for a base period of one (1) year with options up to a total of five (5) years (anticipated execution window: June 2027 through June 2032). 
	  Core Tasks & Frequencies:  
 

 
	  Scheduled Maintenance:  Semi-annual onsite confidence testing and complete inspection (at 6-month intervals). Coordination requires a 20-business-day lead time to request and approve system outages. System inspection includes detectors, agent release/manual pull stations, audible/visual devices, CO2 storage containers, actuator functionality, signal verification to the monitoring station, battery voltage/standby power transfer, and operational/safety training for personnel as requested. 
	  Emergency Trouble Calls:  Provision of up to two (2) emergency trouble calls per contract year. The Contractor must be capable of providing emergency service 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and responding on-site within twenty-four (24) hours of notification. Includes up to eight (8) hours of on-site service, associated travel, and up to $200 in minor repair parts/materials. 
	  Unscheduled Inspection & Repair:  On-call non-emergency repairs and fault corrections identified between scheduled maintenance visits (ordered as firm-fixed-price task orders not to exceed $20,000 across the ordering period). 
	  Reporting & Deliverables:  Submission of comprehensive Service Reports within forty-eight (48) hours of visit completion, documenting compliance with NFPA 12, operational status, test results, and any required follow-on recommendations. Deliverables conform to Data Item Description DI-NDTI-80809 (CDRL A001). 
 

  

 3. MANDATORY CONTRACTOR SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS & SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 

 Interested parties must demonstrate their ability to meet the following mandatory prerequisites: 

 
	  NICET Certification:  Personnel performing inspection, testing, and certification must possess a current National Institute for Certification in Engineering Technologies (NICET) certification in Special Hazards Systems (Level II or above). 
	  ANSUL OEM Training & Authorization:  The Contractor must be formally trained and certified by ANSUL to design, install, test, and maintain carbon dioxide fire suppression systems. The Contractor must also be an authorized ANSUL stocking distributor of clean agent/special hazards equipment to ensure immediate availability of replacement parts
